question: Will the Kennedy Center's main building be open to the general public on October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is closed: main building shut Sept 16, fenced with guards and emergency signage, after the board voted Sept 15 to close for renovations with board materials targeting a summer 2028 reopening. Reference class (venue closed by its own board for multi-year renovation, fenced, layoffs underway) reopens within 2.5 weeks ~5% of the time. Evidence since closure moves further toward NO, not back: a second layoff round began Sept 18, DOJ's Sept 19 filing asks Cooper to lift the injunction and describes running programming at OTHER venues while the main building stays shuttered, and the REACH is being kept open as the memorial-access fig leaf. The only YES hooks are (a) the nominal 7-day safety closure expiring ~Sept 23 and (b) a court-ordered reopening; but the closure is subject to weekly extension by the same executive who declared 'acute risks to public safety' under oath, and Cooper's orders to date bar renaming and major physical changes/demolition while expressly permitting emergency repairs -- he has not ordered reopening, and any such order would likely land late and draw an immediate stay request. I put court-forced access by Oct 2 at ~2-3% and voluntary/partial reopening at ~2-3%. No market matches this contract (the Polymarket/Manifold candidates price demolition announcements, not public access on a date), so no crowd blend.
calls.reference_class: Performing-arts/cultural venues closed to the public by their own governing board with an announced multi-year renovation plan, physical fencing, and concurrent staff layoffs — fraction readmitting the general public within ~2.5 weeks of closure
